source.display_title: 05/28/2026 - João Dantas x Andrew Musial  — Follow Up

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Named three times by the rep: 'Kim gave me some context', 'from Kim, he told me, like, you've been, like, what's been missing is a little bit of structure', and 'I remember Kim asked you, like, you're from Bahia, right?' No suffix in the title.

prospect.name: João Gabriel Dantas
prospect.location: Salvador, Bahia, Brazil — top-floor apartment with a terrace where he trains
prospect.occupation: Physician — private practice plus hospital work, and newly a professor of medicine teaching students and residents
prospect.family_status: Married to a doctor who runs and does CrossFit; a two-year-old daughter and a second daughter due in the last week of October. Recently moved to a larger apartment that is mid-renovation.
prospect.training_background: Calisthenics for several years, weighted calisthenics for close to two. Self-described intermediate athlete — eight to twelve clean pull-ups with 20 kg added, dips with 25 kg. Was 69 kg in his early twenties and built to 86 kg. Moved from high-volume to low-volume work after joint discomfort. Added kettlebells after finding Trevor's YouTube channel and bought one 16 kg bell; ran a 30-minute EMOM of snatches, push-ups, thrusters and pull-ups the day of the call. Trains three to four times a week in 30-40 minute sessions.

signals: Already fit, disciplined and successful — a physician at 13-14% body fat training four to five times a week, wanting to reach 10-12%

Explicitly good-to-great and specific about the gap: 'I was neglecting a lot of stuff in terms of endurance, in terms of VO2 max... Just by having only one goal, so I'm not really satisfied with that'

Validated the price on its merits rather than resisting it: 'I don't think it's an absurd value. And I think for that, for Trevor's work and for the accountability, I think actually that is pretty fair'
Self-identifies discipline as a solved problem: 'I'm a very disciplined guy... discipline is not, it's not a problem'
Departs from the pure type only on liquidity, and for reasons of timing rather than income — a second child due in October, an apartment mid-renovation and a practice being restructured

goals.text: Combine kettlebell work with his existing calisthenics into one coherent structure without overtraining
Build conditioning and VO2 max, the pillars he has neglected by training only for calisthenics strength
Add some muscle mass without becoming a bodybuilder
Drop from 13-14% body fat to 10-12% — not for vanity, because 'when that happened, my training gets a lot better'
Improve mobility, the third pillar calisthenics neglects
Train sustainably for the long run in 30-40 minute sessions around hospital hours and two small children
Have the energy to play with his two daughters
Cut through the noise of the fitness industry with a structure he can just execute — 'My mind works very well when I know exactly what to do'
Build toward Trevor's physique: 'that body, Trevor's body, it's the way I want to be built'

pains.text: Cannot work out how to combine kettlebells and weighted calisthenics without overtraining — 'my great doubts nowadays are how to combine those two steps'
Too much conflicting information in the fitness industry — 'There's a lot of noise in the fitness industry'
Time collapsed by a hospital job, a private practice, a new professorship and a toddler — 'Sometimes I just have half an hour, 40 minutes to work out'
Joint discomfort and stiffness from years of high-volume calisthenics — 'shoulders, upper traps, they are all screaming at the end'
Expects training to be severely impaired around the birth in October — 'sometimes we're two or three days without sleeping well'
Household finances committed to an apartment renovation, a second child, a future nanny and rising school fees, with the practice mid-restructure
USD pricing converts to roughly R$25,000-28,000, which he cannot carry now

objections.raw_quote: I just have to know some things about the value and cost because to me right now things are on a tight budget because of my little girl and the next one that is coming.
objections.rep_response: Noted it and continued the presentation, returning to it after the price was given.

objections.raw_quote: when we make the conversion, the change, the conversion, it's about you're probably something along the lines of 25 to 28,000 I believe... so I don't think I can split that into payments right Now, but it's something that I definitely look forward to do in some time because I don't think it's an absurd value.
objections.rep_response: Isolated it correctly — 'apart from the finances right now, is there anything standing in a way from moving forward?' — then offered the three-month tier at $4,000 and further splits.

objections.raw_quote: August, September, and October will be difficult months for me because my wife will be very pregnant. And the moment that the little princess is gonna come to this world is probably in the last week of October... probably training will be kept to a minimum, or maybe even, I don't know, be severely impaired.
objections.rep_response: First reframed it as the reason accountability exists — 'that's why Trevor is for you there when life gets busy' — which the prospect rejected as a tiredness problem rather than a busyness problem. Then proposed the three-month tier to fit the window before October.

objections.raw_quote: I still have to think about it, man, because the problem is we already committed to a lot of expenses right now due to we moving to a different apartment.
objections.rep_response: Ran the change-question — 'what's going to change between now and sometime in the future?' — asked for a timeframe, then asked what he would be willing to put down today. Accepted a one-month callback when no number came.

objections.raw_quote: I have to take a little moment to think about that and involve the wife because we have a lot of projects now for this year
objections.rep_response: Not addressed at any point. No question about what she would say, no ownership frame, no deposit-and-discuss option.

objections.raw_quote: I have just a concern, not a concern, but a, let's say, a doubt, which is the one about the weighted calisthenics. I just like to go over this again, because I don't really need it to be weighted
objections.rep_response: Answered generically — 'this is tailored to your needs, so whatever you will discuss with Trevor he will build a program around that' — without showing how the two systems combine, which was the prospect's central question all call.

offer.payment_plan_terms: On the $6,000 six-month tier: one-time payment, or two payments of $3,000. Three- and six-payment options exist at a higher total, disclosed explicitly — 'We also have, like, three and six payments, but that's resulting, like, the overall price is higher' and 'six payments would be of $1,200, so the total amount would be $7,200'. On the $4,000 three-month tier: two payments of $2,000 or three payments of $1,500. Usual method stated as credit card.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: Used as the differentiator between tiers: 'with six months, you have a guarantee that you will definitely gain at least 20, it's pounds, so it's going to be like around plus 10 kilos from the baseline that you start with on weight of kettlebells... with three months, we cannot guarantee that, because it's too short.' No terms, conditions, remedy or qualifying requirements were stated, and the metric itself is garbled between pounds and kilos.

prospect_financials.note: No figures given. He declined to name a deposit amount — 'I may be answering something that is not close to reality if I'm going to just give you a value' — and disclosed that the household is not currently able to save, with a practice restructure expected to shorten income for a few months.

evidence: No decision and no commitment: 'I still have to think about it, man' and 'I don't want to commit with you, because I don't really know what's going to happen'
He asked for the callback himself: 'Is there a possibility, Andrew, that I could get in touch with you after some time and maybe we can talk again about this?'
Rep booked a specific follow-up for 29 June at 20:00 Salvador time and exchanged WhatsApp numbers on the call
No payment, no deposit and no payment link — he declined to name any figure he could put down today

Counter-evidence that this is a strong follow-up rather than a soft no: he validated the price unprompted — 'I don't think it's an absurd value... I think actually that is pretty fair' — and named cost as the only blocker
outcome.next_step: Follow-up call on 29 June at 20:00 Brazil time; rep to send a calendar invite and has the prospect's WhatsApp number for the interim.

notable.note: Strongest discovery in the batch and the only call where the rep asked about injuries before recommending anything — no medical risk arises here. Three things a principal should see. First, the prospect independently surfaced the AI texting persona: 'I've been receiving messages like SMS messages from something, from someone named Sophia', and the rep confirmed 'To be honest, it's an AI box' only once asked, adding that the prospect could not reply to it. Second, a results guarantee was asserted to justify the six-month tier over the three-month one — roughly plus 20 lb or 10 kg on kettlebell weight — stated imprecisely and appearing on no other call in this batch. Third, on the same day as the Marian Samson call, the same rep quoted the same financed instalments but here disclosed the uplift plainly ('the overall price is higher... the total amount would be $7,200'), which the earlier call did not.

quality.notes: Labels invert continuously — the rep's entire pillar presentation from about 00:44:06 runs under the prospect's label, and the prospect's own training description at 00:02:36 is split across both speakers. Two long stretches around 00:44:06 and 00:46:57 lose punctuation and speaker breaks entirely. Roles read from content. The rep gives his real first name late in the call: 'it's not Andrew, it's Andrzej, but nobody can pronounce it, so I go by Andrew.'
